3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: We settled on a table on the second floor of Le Papillion, a world class Lespian restaurant in downtown Holsord.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The whole floor was reserved for us, and the music coming from downstairs was enough to guard our voices from potential eavesdroppers.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Nia Morgna had arranged a dinner meeting with Justice Isabel Edmonds. Ahead of the dinner, Nia and I met to have a talk.

6.speaker: Nia Morgna
6.text: "...I still can't believe Soll came to the vote."

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: The waiter approached us and bowed in respect.

11.speaker: Waiter
11.text: "Did you decide on the entrée, sir?"

12.speaker: Player
12.text: "We have a guest coming. We'll wait for her to order."

15.speaker: Player
15.text: "We are in a meeting here. Can you leave us alone?"

20.speaker: Waiter
20.text: "For the entrée, we have the options of sauté-Perlase with Lespian-style Zabla, Falenco-style liver fricassée, or Salade Luco made with fresh vegetables and herbs from southern Lespia."

27.speaker: Nia Morgna
27.text: "No thank you. I'd rather wait for our guest to arrive."

33.speaker: Nia Morgna
33.text: "Let's try not to agitate her when she comes. We won the vote, so she already has pressure on her."

37.speaker: Nia Morgna
37.text: "Not to mention the pressure from the anti-corruption police."

38.speaker: Nia Morgna
38.text: "But if she feels cornered, we might lose her. So it's important not to put too much pressure on her."

40.speaker: Player
40.text: "I disagree. We must keep up the pressure."

43.speaker: Nia Morgna
43.text: "I am not sure about that, Mr. President."

44.speaker: Nia Morgna
44.text: "Just please don't forget that we cannot succeed without her help."

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: At that moment, the waiter came back with my order.

48.speaker: Nia Morgna
48.text: "Oh, Good to see you, Mrs. Edmonds."

49.speaker: Narrator

73.text: He went ahead and refilled our glasses with water.

76.speaker: Nia Morgna
76.text: "Oh, Good to see you, Mrs. Edmonds."

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: Suddenly, I noticed Justice Isabel Edmonds coming upstairs. She was wearing a plain dark gray dress that hid most of her features.

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: Nia got up from her chair to shake Isabel's hand.

81.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
81.text: "Mr. President. Good to see you. I hope you're enjoying your meal."

82.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
82.text: "Mr. President. I hope you're enjoying your meal."

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: The waiter held a chair for Isabel.

88.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
88.text: "No, thank you. I won't be here long."

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: She took a long look at the table and my plate.

93.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
93.text: "Oh no, there's nothing wrong. I just don't want to eat up too much of your time."

94.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
94.text: "I also didn't want to intrude your meal, Mr. President."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "It's okay, Mrs. Edmonds. I thought we were here to meet over a meal."

99.speaker: Narrator
99.text: She stared at me for a second.

103.speaker: Nia Morgna
103.text: "Come on, Mrs. Edmonds. Let's order something."

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: The waiter looked uncomfortable while waiting for the orders.

105.speaker: Nia Morgna
105.text: "I'll have the sauté-Perlase, please. And for Mrs. Edmonds..."

106.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
106.text: "...I'll have the salad, then. Thank you."

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: She took a seat across the table.

111.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
111.text: "I would normally say good, but this time I will take the liberty to say that it was insanely exhausting."

113.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
113.text: "Heavy court matters again... Not that I'm complaining."

115.speaker: Waiter
115.text: "Are you ready to give the orders, sir? Madame?"

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "I'll get the same as Mrs. Morgna."

130.speaker: Waiter
130.text: "For the entrée, we have the options of sauté-Perlase with Lespian-style Zabla, Falenco-style liver fricassée, or Salade Luco made with fresh vegetables and herbs from southern Lespia."

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: He quickly took a couple of notes in his tiny notebook.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: He went back downstairs, leaving us alone on the upper floor again.

140.speaker: Player
140.text: "Mrs. Edmonds. You know why we're here."

141.speaker: Player
141.text: "How is the situation in the Supreme Court?"

142.speaker: Player
142.text: "We want to cooperate with you, Mrs. Edmonds."

143.speaker: Player
143.text: "Let's get to the point, shall we?"

146.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
146.text: "That's very welcome, Mr. President. I want the same thing."

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: She moved herself on the chair to be more comfortable.

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: At that moment, the waiter came back from downstairs, carrying plates of food. After seeing that we were in the midst of a discussion, he averted his eyes as he approached us.

154.speaker: Narrator
154.text: He quickly served Nia and Isabel's food and refilled all of our glasses.

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: He quickly started serving the food and refilled our glasses.

163.speaker: Narrator
163.text: He placed the plate of Falenco-style liver fricassée in front of me. It looked and smelled like heaven.

164.speaker: Narrator
164.text: He placed the plate of Salade Luco in front of me. It looked very fresh and smelled of olive oil.

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: He placed the plate of sauté-Perlase and next to it, the Lespian style Zabla, which was served in a small clay bowl.

173.speaker: Narrator
173.text: The waiter bowed to us and quickly went downstairs.

174.speaker: Narrator
174.text: We wished each other a good meal as Isabel and Nia slowly started to eat.

175.speaker: Nia Morgna
175.text: "So, Mrs. Edmonds... Are you still thinking the same about the Old Guard?"

177.speaker: Nia Morgna
177.text: "That's good. We still have that in common."

178.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
178.text: "That doesn't mean I will accept any proposal the Old Guards oppose..."

179.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
179.text: "...nor it means I will put the whole Court under the bus."

183.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
183.text: "The impeachment clause about the Justices affects all of us, after all."

185.speaker: Nia Morgna
185.text: "You also know that we need this change in our institutions."

186.speaker: Nia Morgna
186.text: "I understand your concerns. I also do not agree with that clause."

187.speaker: Nia Morgna
187.text: "But we must start somewhere. I am supporting the President because he made this proposal with good intentions."

188.speaker: Narrator
188.text: Isabel took a sip from her water and turned to me.

192.speaker: Player
192.text: "Please, Isabel. This vote means a lot to us."

193.speaker: Player
193.text: "Mrs. Edmonds, I really hope you vote for the proposal."

198.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
198.text: "I think I can get behind this proposal."

199.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
199.text: "I regret to say I do not see eye to eye with you, Mr. President. I don't think I can support this proposal."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "Please reconsider, Mrs. Edmonds. This proposal is very important."

201.speaker: Player
201.text: "That's very sad to hear. Is there no way to change your mind?"

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "Look, I will be clear. Whatever you think about it, you will vote yes!"

211.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
211.text: "I can get you the three votes you need."

212.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
212.text: "I think I can get you the votes you need."

214.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
214.text: "I don't think my conclusion will differ."

216.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
216.text: "In fact, I think it's time that I leave."

217.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
217.text: "I see that we're all finished with our meals too. I think it's time to conclude this meeting."

218.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
218.text: "Thank you for inviting me here, Mr. President."

219.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
219.text: "I'll do my best to convince my group. But I can only speak for myself."

220.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
220.text: "We were already somewhat inclined to vote for the proposal. I will talk with my group."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "Are you sure that you can bring three votes?"

224.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
224.text: "Yes. We always act together. They will listen to me."

227.speaker: Player
227.text: "So you are not sure if you can bring three votes?"

228.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
228.text: "I told you that I will speak with them. What else would you want me to do?"

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: Isabel took her coat and walked downstairs. Nia and I looked at each other.

232.speaker: Nia Morgna
232.text: "That's great to hear that you will support us. Thank you."

234.speaker: Player
234.text: "Don't disrespect me like this, Mrs. Edmonds."

236.speaker: Player
236.text: "You can't leave before we agree on this."

238.speaker: Narrator
238.text: She stood up and shook my hand.

239.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
239.text: "I don't know what you mean. I have already told you my position. And I have another place to be, Mr. President."

241.speaker: Nia Morgna
241.text: "Thank you for the meeting, Mrs. Edmonds."

243.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
243.text: "I see that we're all finished with our meals too. I think it's time to conclude this meeting."

244.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
244.text: "Thank you for inviting me here, Mr. President."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "I'll be expecting your vote in the upcoming session."

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: She stood up and shook my hand.

249.speaker: Nia Morgna
249.text: "Thank you for the meeting, Mrs. Edmonds."

255.speaker: Nia Morgna
255.text: "You should maybe talk to Lucian about other options. We may need to reach out to Heron, but I don't think he'll be of any help without Isabel."

257.speaker: Narrator
257.text: After a few minutes of thoughtful silence, we also got up from our seats and left the restaurant.

258.speaker: Narrator
258.text: Isabel took her coat and walked downstairs. Nia and I looked at each other.

260.speaker: Player
260.text: "Yes. I hope we can trust her."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "We still need to reach out to more people. She won't be enough."

263.speaker: Nia Morgna
263.text: "You should maybe talk to Lucian about other options. We may try reaching out to Heron if you want."

264.speaker: Narrator
264.text: After a few minutes of thoughtful silence, we also got up from our seats and left the restaurant.

268.speaker: Nia Morgna
268.text: "No, thank you. I'll be leaving soon."

272.speaker: Nia Morgna
272.text: "No thank you. I'll be leaving soon."

277.speaker: Nia Morgna
277.text: "I know it's too late, but you are making a mistake. You've sent our opportunity to change the constitution for the better right into the trash."

278.speaker: Nia Morgna
278.text: "And I can't believe that you also..."

286.speaker: Narrator
286.text: She shook our hands and left the room.

287.speaker: Nia Morgna
287.text: "Have a nice evening, Mr. President. Mrs. Edmonds."

288.speaker: Narrator
288.text: She shook our hands and left the room.

289.speaker: Nia Morgna
289.text: "Have a nice evening, Mr. President. Mrs. Edmonds."

290.speaker: Nia Morgna
290.text: "I won't be ordering. I was just leaving."

298.speaker: Nia Morgna
298.text: "But now that you are here, I will take my leave. I have business to take care of."

302.speaker: Narrator
302.text: He quickly served Isabel's food and refilled our glasses.

308.speaker: Narrator
308.text: We wished each other a good meal as Isabel started to eat.

309.speaker: Narrator
309.text: The food here was insanely delicious.

322.speaker: Narrator
322.text: Isabel took her coat and walked downstairs.

329.speaker: Narrator
329.text: It was not a good start. It looked like I had no choice but to work with the Old Guards if I wanted to pass this Constitution.

330.speaker: Narrator
330.text: It was a good start. But I was still uncertain if Isabel would be enough.

331.speaker: Narrator
331.text: It was time to think about the other options if I wanted to pass this Constitution.

333.speaker: Narrator
333.text: I got in the presidential Kadilla and Serge started driving me home.

337.speaker: Narrator
337.text: On the way, I received a call on the brand new radio phone that was mounted in our vehicle.

341.speaker: Narrator
341.text: On the way, I received a call from on the brand new radio phone that was mounted in our vehicle.

342.speaker: Narrator
342.text: It was Kesaro Kibener. His voice was very difficult to understand through the static.

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: It was Lucian. His voice was very difficult to understand through the static.

344.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
344.text: "Mr. President. I hope your meeting went well."

345.speaker: Lucian Galade
345.text: "Mr. President. I hope your meeting went well."

346.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
346.text: "I have some good news for you."

347.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
347.text: "Mr. Garaci had agreed to meet with you. As long as the meeting is not documented and kept hidden."

348.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
348.text: "I will try to arrange something. Would you be able to meet with him outside of the capital? He said it would be safer."

349.speaker: Lucian Galade
349.text: "I have urgent news to share. Heron has agreed to meet before the Court Vote."

350.speaker: Lucian Galade
350.text: "He wants to arrange a meeting outside of the capital. Somewhere more hidden and out of the public eye."

352.speaker: Player
352.text: "That's good news. I'll leave the arrangement up to you."

354.speaker: Lucian Galade
354.text: "Sir, are you sure? He'd be very helpful."

357.speaker: Player
357.text: "Okay, I'll leave it to your judgement."

359.speaker: Lucian Galade
359.text: "Understood, sir. Then I'll try to arrange a meeting."

364.speaker: Player
364.text: "That's good news. I'll leave the arrangement up to you."

366.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
366.text: "What do you mean? I thought you wanted me to convince him."

368.speaker: Player
368.text: "You're right. Okay, I'll leave the arrangement to your judgement, Kesaro."

369.speaker: Player
369.text: "Yes, I did. But the meeting has to be on my terms. Is he not willing to meet in Holsord?"

370.speaker: Player
370.text: "He's either going to come to my office or we won't have a meeting."

371.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
371.text: "I'm afraid that won't do for him."

373.speaker: Player
373.text: "Then force him. I thought you were supposed to convince him."

375.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
375.text: "I'll let you return to your duties now. Good evening."

377.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
377.text: "I already did. You are asking for too much."

378.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
378.text: "Anyway, I'll leave you to your duties. Good evening."

412.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
412.text: "I'll do my best to get the three votes but I can only speak for myself."

413.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
413.text: "Your changes to Article 6 and 7 will make it really difficult."

416.speaker: Player
416.text: "So you are not sure if you can bring three votes?"

417.speaker: Isabel Edmonds
417.text: "Maybe you should have thought about this before you altered your proposal at the last minute."
